fuente.nota: Text shortened by paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: Coffee is a caffeinated drink prepared from roasted coffee beans. It's also a plant (Coffea) and the name of the drink that is made from this plant. The coffee plant is a bush or tree that can grow up to ten meters (about 32 feet) high, but is usually cut shorter. Coffee plants originally grew in Ethiopia, and now also grow in South America, Central America, Southeast Asia and Turkey. They are an important crop for the economies of many countries.
The drink is made from the seeds of the coffee plant, called coffee beans. Coffee is usually served hot, and is a popular drink in many countries.

To make a drink from coffee beans, the beans must first be specially prepared by drying the beans and then roasting. The beans are dried a short time after they are picked. This preserves them and makes them ready to be packed or roasted. Before the beans are made into a drink, they must be roasted and ground (crushed into tiny pieces in a coffee mill). When the ground coffee is placed into boiling water, the flavour and dark brown colour of the beans goes into the water. Making coffee is called brewing coffee. There are several different ways that coffee can be brewed.

There are two main types of coffee plants: coffea arabica and coffea robusta. Arabica is the most common. Most of the world's coffee is made from Arabica beans Robusta is easier to grow in places where Arabica will not grow.

Robusta is cheaper and has more caffeine than Arabica and it is used in many commercial coffee products. But Robusta tastes bitter and acidic, so people only drink it with other things. Better quality Robustas are in some espresso blends.

In the past, people gave names to new Arabica coffees from the port they came from. The two oldest Arabica coffees are "Mocha" and "Java". Today, names are more specific. They tell us the country, region, and sometimes even the property where they come from.

The traditional way to plant coffee is to put 20 seeds in a hole at the beginning of the rainy season. However, in this way about 50% of the seeds are wasted. They do not sprout. In Brazil, farmers grow coffee in a better way. They grow seedlings in nurseries. After six to twelve months, they move the young plants outside. Coffee is often grown along with other food crops such as corn, beans, or rice for a few years. This lets farmers get used to what coffee plants need to grow well. Coffee plants grow in the area between the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn. This part of the world is called the bean belt or coffee belt.

Single-origin coffee is a term to describe the coffee varieties that are organically grown in a specific geographical area. For this reason, the overall quality of single-origin coffee is attributed to the agroecological factors in the coffee plantations. External agro ecological factors such as altitudes, temperatures, and quality of the soil are the most significant determiners that play a role in flavor note formation for the green coffee beans inside the coffee cherries.

Most of the time, single-origin coffee is the top-notch arabica varieties like Gayo Sumatra, Ethiopian Yirgacheffe, Lintong Sumatra, Kenya AA, and more varieties going on the list. However, premium-grade robusta can be considered single-origin varieties as long as it grows under ideal growing conditions.

Some sorts of coffee taste better if the beans are aged. This means that after they are picked, the beans are dried and then kept from three to eight years. This "aging" gives the coffee a less acidic taste. Coffee that has been aged is often mixed or "blended" with other coffee that is not aged.
Roasting is one of the important stages in making coffee beans into coffee. When a coffee bean is roasted, it grows nearly two times bigger and changes from green to yellow to brown.

The length of time that the coffee beans are roasted makes the coffee taste different. Some types of coffee, such as Mocha and Java, are roasted for a short time. It is easy to tell from the flavour where the coffee is from. When coffee is roasted for a long time, it is harder to tell the different types apart. Green coffee beans can be bought and roasted at home in the oven.

Before the coffee is made into a drink, it is ground in a small grinding machine called a coffee mill. The coffee mill breaks the beans into very small pieces. Coffee is turned into a drink in several different ways. For some ways of making coffee, such as espresso, it is best to have the coffee ground into fine powder. or other types of coffee-making, such as filtered coffee, the coffee is in larger pieces to stop it going through the filter. Finely ground coffee makes a stronger taste.

Boiling: The coffee and the water are put into a pot on top of the stove and boiled slowly together. This way of making coffee has been used for hundreds of years. It is the way that coffee is usually made in the Middle East, North Africa, Turkey and Greece.

Pressure: The boiling water is forced through the ground coffee by a machine. This type of coffee is called Espresso and the machine is called an "Espresso machine" or "Coffee system". Espresso machines are often found in cafes and restaurants. Espresso is a very strong coffee that can be used to make other coffee drinks.

Gravity: Filtered coffee is made by gravity because the boiling water falls from a machine onto the coffee. The coffee grounds are held in a paper or metal "filter" that the water can run through, but the little coffee pieces cannot. The water becomes coloured and flavoured as it runs through the coffee and into a coffee pot.

Steeping: Boiling water is poured onto the coffee and it is allowed to stand for a little while, until the water has taken the colour and flavour. This is often done in a cafetière, which is a tall glass or coffee pot which has a special filter inside that can be pushed down when the coffee is ready so that the person does not drink the coffee grounds. Another way of steeping coffee is to have coffee grounds in a small packet, the right size to make one cup of coffee. The packet is placed in the cup and water poured over it. Then the packet is removed.

Cappuccino is espresso with frothed milk (milk mixed with air). A well-made cappuccino should be made of strong coffee. When the frothy milk is poured gently into the coffee cup, it should be white on top and have a ring of darker coffee around the edge. Cappuccino coffee sometimes has cocoa sprinkled on top.
Flat white is a double espresso where milk micro foam is added to the crema (an emulsion of the oils in the coffee beans when combined with hot water that floats) on the double espresso.
Vietnamese style coffee (Cafe Sua Da) is filtered coffee poured over ice into a glass with sweet condensed milk (thick milk which has had the water removed).
Frappé has several meanings. It is a mix of instant coffee, milk, sugar, and foam. Another form of the drink is blended frozen coffee. And the last is a milkshake, a thick milkshake.

"Instant coffee" is a very quick way to make a cup of coffee to drink. It is made in a factory and sold in jars or packets. First, strong coffee is made using ground coffee and boiling water. Then, the coffee grounds are filtered out. The coffee liquid is dried out until nothing is left except granules (little crunchy pieces), or fine powder. This is then put into jars or packets. As soon as a spoonful of "instant coffee" is added to boiling water, it dissolves in the water to make coffee to drink. The taste can be very different from fresh coffee. Part of the reason for the different taste is that Robusta coffee beans are usually used for making instant coffee. Robusta coffee beans do not cost as much as Arabica.
Coffee is also sold, hot or cold, in cans and bottles. It is ready to drink. It is sold in vending machines and convenience stores with other soft drinks.

The United States buys the most coffee; Germany is next. People in Finland drink the most coffee for each person. In Canada, the United States and Europe, some restaurants sell mainly coffee; they are referred to as "cafés" or "coffeehouses". Cafés often sell food, but the type of food is different from one country to another.

In many countries, people drink coffee at work; in the United States and England, for example, people drink it in the morning. In other countries, such as Mexico, people drink it in the evening to help them stay awake.
Coffee contains the drug caffeine. Caffeine is a mild stimulant which helps to keep people awake. Caffeine, like many drugs, can be addictive and can cause health problems.

Consuming high amounts of caffeine may increase the risk of anxiety, especially among people with panic disorder or social anxiety disorder. Less commonly, it may trigger mania and psychosis in those who are susceptible.

Some studies have looked at the health risks of coffee. In February 2003, there was a study in Denmark of 18,478 women to find out if coffee had an effect on pregnancy and birth. It was found that if a woman drank between four and seven cups of coffee a day, it did not seem to make a big change to the number of babies that were born dead, (stillborn). But the women in the study who drank eight or more cups of coffee a day had three times as much chance of having a stillborn baby.
resumen_es: Popular-science text about coffee: the plant and its varieties, cultivation, ageing, roasting, grinding and brewing methods, the best-known drinks, consumption in different countries and its possible health effects.

ideas_clave.idea: Coffee is both a plant, native to Ethiopia and now grown in several regions where it is economically important, and the hot drink made from its seeds.
Before it can be drunk, coffee must be dried, roasted, ground and then brewed in water, which can be done in several ways.
There are two main species: Arabica, the most widespread, and Robusta, which is cheaper and stronger in caffeine but bitter; coffee names now indicate a precise origin.
Traditional planting wastes many seeds, whereas Brazilian growers raise seedlings in nurseries; coffee only grows in the tropical 'bean belt'.
Single-origin coffee comes from one specific area, and its quality depends on local conditions such as altitude, temperature and soil.
Some beans are stored for several years to reduce their acidity and are often blended with younger coffee.
During roasting the beans swell and darken, and the length of roasting changes the flavour and how easily the origin can be recognised.
The beans are ground more or less finely depending on the preparation method, and finer grinding gives a stronger taste.
The four main brewing methods are boiling, pressure (espresso), gravity (filter coffee) and steeping, for instance in a cafetière.
Popular variations include cappuccino, flat white, Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk, and frappé.
Instant coffee is dried into granules or powder in factories and tastes different, partly because it is made with Robusta; coffee is also sold ready to drink.
The United States buys the most coffee and Finland drinks the most per person, while habits about where and when people drink it vary between countries.
Caffeine is a mild but addictive stimulant; high doses may increase anxiety, and a Danish study linked very high consumption during pregnancy to a greater risk of stillbirth.

resumen_modelo: The text explains that coffee is both a plant, originally from Ethiopia and now cultivated in many tropical regions, and the popular drink made from its seeds, known as beans. Before being consumed, the beans have to be dried, roasted, ground and finally brewed in hot water. There are two main species: Arabica, which accounts for most of the world's production, and Robusta, which is cheaper and contains more caffeine but has a bitter taste. Cultivation methods also matter; for instance, Brazilian farmers raise seedlings in nurseries rather than sowing seeds directly, and single-origin coffees owe their quality to local conditions such as altitude and soil. The flavour is further shaped by ageing, which reduces acidity, by the length of roasting, since a long roast makes different origins harder to distinguish, and by how finely the beans are ground, finer grinding producing a stronger taste. The text then describes four ways of preparing the drink, namely boiling, pressure, as in espresso, gravity, as in filter coffee, and steeping, before listing popular drinks such as cappuccino or Vietnamese iced coffee. It also mentions instant and ready-to-drink coffee, which taste different from freshly brewed coffee, partly because instant coffee is usually made from cheaper Robusta beans. As far as consumption is concerned, the United States imports the most coffee, whereas Finns drink the most per person, and drinking habits vary between countries, with some people drinking it in the morning and others in the evening. Finally, the text warns that caffeine is an addictive stimulant: high doses may increase anxiety, and a Danish study found that women who drank eight or more cups a day during pregnancy faced a higher risk of stillbirth.

It is the most common type of coffee
It is always aged before roasting

preguntas.cita: Robusta is cheaper and has more caffeine than Arabica and it is used in many commercial coffee products.
preguntas.explicacion: The text highlights its lower price and higher caffeine content. It is bitter, not sweet, and the most common variety is Arabica.

preguntas.explicacion: The text attributes quality to the agro-ecological factors of the plantation. Roasting, grinding and brewing affect the flavour, but they are not mentioned here; the port was the old criterion for naming coffee.
